My lens already carries the price analogue ('a weekend carrying a contract roll passes the leg change as never-traded'); this is the FLOW analogue and I believe it is new. Falsifier: an expiry-Friday seam where the deferred leg's big-print buy share is elevated AND the session's aggregate signed flow is materially positive rather than a wash - that would show conviction surviving the confound. n=1 here, PROPOSED only.

cross_cutting_finding: Two things this day taught that generalise. (1) A weekend seam whose Friday carries a contract EXPIRY confounds that Friday's exit tells on the SURVIVING leg: the roll SELLS the expiring contract and BUYS the deferred, and the deferred is the leg we score - so big_print_b_share and the final-phase net both read spuriously BULLISH. On 0626 the confounded fields (0.783 big prints, +2,737 final phase on 64% of session volume) sat on top of an aggregate that was a WASH (+871 on 121,487 lots, two-sided 0.504), and the aggregate is what tells you the bullish tells were mechanical. This is the flow analogue of the price-seam rule already in my lens, and it is the same species as data hole #8: a well-formed, self-consistent number computed on the right instrument that still carries a false mechanism - only comparing it against an INDEPENDENT quantity (here the session aggregate) settles it. (2) The forward weather ladder being HDD-only is not merely an inconvenience in a July block - it is structurally worse at the SUNDAY REOPEN than anywhere else, because the only CDD-bearing channel sits behind a D-1T23:59Z asof wall that falls two hours AFTER the gap prints, while the one pre-reopen limb carries no CDD at all. In a summer block the DIRECTION of a weekend heat add is defensible pre-reopen from two-model agreement and the SIZE is not measurable at all. Every summer weekend gap in this walk inherits that hole.
